items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Understanding the Organization and Its Context
items.intent: The organization knows the outside and inside issues that affect what its QMS is for, and it keeps watching them.
items.question: How do you identify the external and internal issues that affect your maintenance QMS, and how often do you review them?
evidence: Documented context analysis or issue register with a review date
Records of the last review and decisions taken
failure_modes: Issues identified once and never reviewed

items.title: Understanding the Needs and Expectations of Interested Parties
items.intent: Relevant interested parties and their requirements are identified and monitored, including customer and regulatory requirements.
items.question: Who are your relevant interested parties, including the competent authority, and what do they require?
evidence: Records of monitoring, such as authority or customer correspondence
failure_modes: Requirements not reflected in the QMS

items.title: Determining the Scope of the Quality Management System
items.intent: The QMS scope states the products and services covered, the approvals held, and justifies any requirement judged not applicable.
items.question: What does your QMS scope cover, including the approvals and ratings you hold, and how did you justify any exclusion?
evidence: Documented scope with products, services and approvals stated
Justification for each exclusion, linked to the quality manual
failure_modes: Scope omits an approval or rating

items.title: Quality Management System and Its Processes
items.intent: The QMS is run as connected processes, including the regulatory approvals, certificates and ratings the organization must satisfy.
items.question: Show how your processes are identified and how they meet the approvals, certificates and ratings you hold.
evidence: Process map with inputs, outputs and owners
Cross-reference of processes to approvals and ratings
failure_modes: Approvals or ratings not reflected in the processes

items.title: QMS processes: establishment, operation and improvement
items.intent: Processes have defined inputs, outputs, criteria, resources, responsibilities, risk handling and improvement, and address customer and regulatory requirements including approvals, certificates, ratings, capability list and licences.
items.question: For one maintenance process, walk me through its inputs, outputs, criteria, resources, responsibilities and how it meets regulatory requirements.
evidence: Link to the capability list or ratings
failure_modes: Regulatory requirements not addressed by the process

items.title: Documented information for the QMS
items.intent: Documented information supports the processes, including the description of the system that records the work done on each article or product.
items.question: Show the documented description of your QMS and the system you use to record work on each article.
evidence: Quality manual or equivalent covering all required elements
Work record system description for articles or products
Records that processes run as planned
failure_modes: No record system for work on each article
Required element missing from the quality manual

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Leadership and Commitment
items.intent: Top management takes visible responsibility for the QMS, including its safety policy and timely corrective action from audits.
items.question: How does top management show accountability, safety commitment, and the timely closure of audit corrective actions?

items.title: General
items.intent: Top management ensures policy and objectives, integration into business processes, the process approach, resources, communication, improvement, the safety policy and safety objectives, and timely corrective action.
items.question: Give me this year's examples of top management acting on each leadership element, including safety.
failure_modes: Corrective actions not implemented in due time

items.title: Customer Focus
items.intent: Customer and regulatory requirements are determined and met, and conformity and on-time delivery are measured with action when targets are missed.
items.question: How do you know customer and regulatory requirements are met, and what happens when on-time delivery falls short?
evidence: Action records when targets are missed

items.title: Policy
items.intent: The quality policy exists and is communicated.
items.question: Show me your quality policy and how it is communicated and understood.

items.title: Establishing the Quality Policy
items.intent: The policy suits the organization, frames objectives, commits to meeting requirements, and commits to continual improvement.
items.question: Show where the policy commits to requirements and to continual improvement.
failure_modes: Commitment to requirements or improvement missing

items.title: Communicating the Quality Policy
items.intent: The policy is documented, communicated, understood and available to relevant parties.
items.question: How is the policy made available and understood by the people who maintain aircraft?
evidence: Document control record of the policy

items.title: Establishing and Communicating the Safety Policy
items.intent: A safety policy sets a framework for safety objectives, encourages safety reporting without punitive action, and commits to continual safety improvement. It is kept as documented information.
items.question: Show your safety policy, and how staff are told they can report safety concerns without punishment.
evidence: Documented safety policy with reporting statement and improvement commitment
Safety reporting procedure and examples of reports handled
failure_modes: Reporting statement missing or staff fear punishment

items.title: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities
items.intent: Roles and authorities are assigned and understood, and a management representative has oversight and unrestricted access to top management. Required key management positions are appointed.
items.question: Who is the management representative and the key management positions, and what authority does each hold?
evidence: Appointment records for the management representative and key positions

items.title: Accountable Manager
items.intent: The Accountable Manager has overall financial and corporate responsibility for the approval scope and ensures continuing airworthiness activities can be financed and carried out to standard.
items.question: Who holds the Accountable Manager role, and how do they know maintenance can be financed and carried out to standard?
evidence: Direct reporting line to the top executive where the Accountable Manager and the top executive are different people

items.title: Quality Manager
items.intent: A Quality Manager monitors the QMS, runs an independent audit programme, reports quality feedback to the Accountable Manager, and has direct access to them.
items.question: Who is your Quality Manager, how is the audit programme kept independent, and how do you report quality feedback to the Accountable Manager?
evidence: Quality feedback reports to the Accountable Manager
failure_modes: No direct access to the Accountable Manager

items.title: Other Appointed Manager(s)
items.intent: Managers are appointed to make sure operational activities meet customer and authority requirements in each major area, and they are answerable to the Accountable Manager.
items.question: Which managers oversee each major area of activity, and to whom do they answer?
evidence: Reporting lines to the Accountable Manager
failure_modes: Major area without an appointed manager

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities
items.intent: Risks and opportunities for the QMS are identified and addressed.
items.question: What are the main risks and opportunities for your maintenance QMS, and what did you do about each?

items.title: Planning for risks and opportunities
items.intent: Planning considers context and interested party requirements, to assure results, enhance desirable effects, prevent undesired effects, and improve.
items.question: Show how context and interested party requirements fed into your risk planning.
evidence: Planning record citing context and interested party inputs

items.title: Planned actions and their effectiveness
items.intent: Actions are integrated into processes, checked for effectiveness, and proportionate to their impact on conformity.
items.question: Pick one risk action: how was it integrated into a process, and how did you test it worked?

items.title: Quality Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
items.intent: Measurable quality objectives exist at relevant functions and levels, and they are planned and monitored.
items.question: Show your quality objectives, their owners, and how progress is tracked.

items.title: Quality objectives
items.intent: Objectives are consistent with the policy, measurable, reflect applicable requirements and customer satisfaction, are monitored, communicated and updated, and are kept as documented information.
items.question: Choose one objective and show it meets each property.
evidence: Objective record with measure, target, owner and review date
failure_modes: Objective not consistent with the policy

items.title: Planning how to achieve objectives
items.intent: For each objective the organization records what will be done, the resources, the person responsible, the completion date and how results are evaluated.
items.question: For one objective, show the plan with all five elements.
evidence: Objective action plan with all five elements
failure_modes: Plan missing an owner or date

items.title: Planning of Changes
items.intent: QMS changes are planned and consider their purpose and consequences, QMS integrity, resources, responsibilities, and the risks during transition.
items.question: Describe the last QMS change and how you planned it, including risks during transition.
evidence: Change plan covering the required considerations

items.note: Top-level clause. Title not extracted from the licensed copy (structure line only).

items.title: Resources
items.intent: Resources needed for the QMS are determined and provided.
items.question: How do you decide what resources the QMS needs?

items.title: General
items.intent: Resources are determined, including tools, equipment, maintenance data, facilities, materials and qualified people available when tasks are done, to ensure safe completion of activities.
items.question: For one maintenance task, show that tools, data, facilities and qualified people were available when the task was done.
evidence: Current maintenance data at point of work
failure_modes: Task started without required tools or current data

items.title: People
items.intent: The right people are in place to run the QMS and its processes.
items.question: How do you confirm you have enough qualified people for each process?

items.title: Infrastructure
items.intent: Buildings, equipment, transport and information systems needed for processes and conformity are provided and maintained, and serviceable is segregated from unserviceable and aviation from non-aviation as required.
items.question: Show how serviceable and unserviceable articles are segregated, and how maintenance equipment is kept serviceable.
failure_modes: Unserviceable articles mixed with serviceable stock

items.title: Environment for the Operation of Processes
items.intent: The working environment, human and physical, is set so processes and conformity are achieved.
items.question: What environmental conditions matter to your maintenance processes, and how are they monitored?
failure_modes: Environment undefined where it affects conformity

items.title: Monitoring and Measuring Resources
items.intent: Monitoring and measuring resources give valid results.
items.question: How do you make sure your measuring resources give valid results?

items.title: General
items.intent: Monitoring and measurement resources suit their use, are maintained, and their fitness for purpose is documented.
items.question: For one measuring resource, show that it suits its use and remains fit for purpose.
failure_modes: No evidence of fitness for purpose

items.title: Measurement Traceability
items.intent: Measuring equipment is calibrated or verified against traceable standards at set intervals or before use, identified for status, safeguarded from adjustment, recalled when due, and recorded in a register. When equipment is found unfit, the validity of past results is reviewed.
items.question: Pick one calibrated instrument: show its certificate, its status label, its register entry, and what you checked when it was last found out of tolerance.
evidence: Calibration certificate traceable to national or international standards
Register entry with type, ID, location, method, frequency and acceptance criteria
Review of past results after an out-of-tolerance finding
failure_modes: Past results not reviewed after out-of-tolerance finding

items.title: Organizational Knowledge
items.intent: Knowledge needed for processes and conformity is determined, kept, made available, and updated as needs change.
items.question: What critical knowledge does the maintenance organization depend on, and how is it kept when people leave?

items.title: Competence
items.intent: People doing work that affects the QMS are competent. Those performing maintenance, including certifying staff, are identified, qualified and certified per the competent authority, kept current through initial and recurrent training, and non-qualified persons are supervised before working unsupervised.
items.question: Show how a certifying staff member is qualified, kept current, and how a new person is assessed before they work unsupervised.
evidence: Certifying staff qualification and authorization records
Assessment record for a non-qualified person before unsupervised work
Documented information on persons performing maintenance
failure_modes: Certifying staff not qualified or not current
Unsupervised work by an unassessed person

items.title: Awareness
items.intent: People know the policy, objectives, their contribution, the consequences of nonconformity, product safety, ethics, the safety policy and objectives, and the human factors that affect maintenance.
items.question: Pick a technician: what can they tell you about human factors and product safety in their work?
failure_modes: Staff cannot describe human factors risks in their work

items.title: Communication
items.intent: Internal and external communications are planned, including promotion of product safety information.
items.question: Show your communication plan and an example of safety information being promoted to staff.

items.title: Documented Information
items.intent: The QMS has the documented information it requires, including for product safety management, and it is controlled.
items.question: How do you decide the documented information the QMS and product safety management need?

items.title: General
items.intent: The QMS includes required documented information, information needed for its effectiveness, and information needed for product safety management.
items.question: Show the required documented information against the standard's list, and the product safety documents you keep.
